unsure: Binders nested inside the info are still collected for the whole type rather than scoped to their binder, so a nested type parameter or existential used outside its own binder elsewhere in the same info is still hidden (the same imprecision retronym/scala#459 has for existentials). The outermost type parameters go through the existing owner check, which accepts parameters owned by any enclosing definition, not only by the symbol itself. A genuine report on a huge type still renders the signature in full before truncating, once per tree.
note: Only PolyTypes nested inside the checked info bind their type parameters; the info's own outermost PolyType parameters go through the owner check, so a method whose info reuses another method's type parameters is reported again. New JUnit test mutates a typed tree to show that report and asserts no report for a lub and a refinement with a polymorphic member.
